sources.entry: Cryptomator - Multi-platform transparent client-side encryption of your files in the cloud.

summary.one_liner: Cryptomator is an open-source desktop app that transparently encrypts files on the client side before they are stored in cloud-synced folders.
summary.what_it_does: Cryptomator creates encrypted vaults inside a local directory that a cloud sync service (such as Dropbox, Google Drive, or OneDrive) then uploads. Users open a vault through a virtual drive and work with files as if on a USB drive, while file contents and file names are encrypted with AES-256 and folder structure is obfuscated. The README says it uses scrypt key derivation, authenticated encryption for file content, and per-file information needed for decryption, with no accounts or metadata shared with an online service. Each vault can have its own password. The README describes building from source with Maven and JDK 26, and running it via a Maven profile; native binaries are offered on cryptomator.org.
use_cases: encrypt files before uploading to Dropbox or Google Drive
protect cloud-synced folders with a password
keep sensitive documents private in OneDrive or Nextcloud
create multiple separately password-protected encrypted vaults
work on encrypted files through a virtual drive
how_to_run: Optional development run with separate settings: ./mvnw -Prun,dev compile exec:exec
Or download native binaries from cryptomator.org
notable: Transparent virtual drive: use files as on a USB stick while encryption happens behind the scenes
Works with any cloud service that syncs a local directory, per the README
Encrypts file names and obfuscates folder structure
Client-side design with no accounts and no online service involved
Dual-licensed: GPLv3 for FOSS, commercial license available
caveats: Depends on donations and sponsorship for ongoing development, per the README
Commercial use under different terms requires contacting the team (dual license)
Building from source requires JDK 26 and Maven
keywords: share files with my team securely
